extraction.name: CommonsenseQA
extraction.description: A challenging dataset for commonsense question answering designed to test the ability of models to leverage prior knowledge beyond surface-level associations. The dataset consists of 12,247 multiple-choice questions generated by crowd workers using concepts and relations from CONCEPTNET, requiring complex semantics and background knowledge to answer correctly.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.publisher: School of Computer Science, Tel-Aviv University and Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
extraction.citeAs: Talmor, A., Herzig, J., Lourie, N., & Berant, J. (2019). CommonsenseQA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge. arXiv preprint arXiv:1811.00937.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Crowd workers authored multiple-choice questions based on subgraphs extracted from CONCEPTNET, where each subgraph contained a source concept and three target concepts sharing the same semantic relation. Workers created questions that required commonsense knowledge to distinguish the correct target concept from distractors. Additional distractors were added by selecting from CONCEPTNET or manually authored by workers. Web snippets were retrieved via Google search to provide textual context for each question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Crowdsourcing, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CONCEPTNET knowledge base, which contains 32 million triplets of commonsense knowledge (e.g., (gambler, CapableOf, lose money)).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Triplets from CONCEPTNET were filtered to exclude general relations (e.g., RelatedTo) or those already well-explored in NLP. Triplets with concepts exceeding four words or not in English were removed. Triplets with low edit distance between concepts were also filtered. This resulted in 236,208 triplets, from which 130,000 triplets (43,000 question sets) were selected for question generation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers were asked to author three questions per subgraph (one per target concept), ensuring the question contained the source concept and discriminated between the target concepts. Workers were instructed to avoid surface clues and to add two additional distractors per question (one from CONCEPTNET and one manually authored). Questions were verified by a separate group of workers, who annotated them as unanswerable or selected the correct answer. Only questions verified by at least one worker who answered correctly were included.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were verified by two workers, and only those verified by at least one worker who answered correctly were included. This process filtered out 15% of the questions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available for download at http://www.tau-nlp.org/commonsenseqa, and the code for baselines is available at https://github.com/jonathanherzig/commonsenseqa. No explicit versioning or deprecation policies are mentioned.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance research in commonsense reasoning, which is critical for natural language understanding systems. It highlights the gap between human performance and machine performance in tasks requiring commonsense knowledge, emphasizing the need for further research in this area.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may inherit biases from CONCEPTNET, which is a knowledge base created by human contributors. Additionally, the crowd-sourcing process may introduce biases based on the demographics and perspectives of the workers involved in question generation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset focuses on commonsense knowledge derived from CONCEPTNET, which may not capture all forms of commonsense reasoning. The questions are generated by crowd workers, which may introduce variability in question quality and complexity. The dataset does not include explicit context for many questions, relying instead on the commonsense knowledge of the reader. Models trained on this dataset may struggle with questions requiring nuanced or culturally specific commonsense knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-Tuning for commonsense question answering models. The dataset is designed to evaluate the ability of models to leverage prior knowledge and perform well on questions that require complex semantics and background knowledge.
